title: Review of Conditions in Migrant Worker Dormitories following Incident at Westlite Jalan Tukang Dormitory
what_it_is: Review of Conditions in Migrant Worker Dormitories following Incident at Westlite Jalan Tukang Dormitory

sections.label: Westlite Jalan Tukang Dormitory conditions
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Manpower about aid response, causes of unsatisfactory conditions, and resources for hygiene, food and medical standards in dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) why was a foreign embassy able to respond more quickly than the dormitory operator or the Ministry with the provision of aid and support to foreign workers residing at the Westlite Jalan Tukang Dormitory; (b) what acts can be ascribed to the dormitory operator or other stakeholders that resulted in the unsatisfactory conditions at the dormitory; and (c) whether there are sufficient resources deployed to ensure minimum standards of hygiene, food quality and medical support at all foreign worker dormitories in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the findings on the allegations of poor living conditions at Westlite Dormitory at Jalan Tukang; (b) what actions has the Ministry taken to rectify the issues; and (c) what are the measures taken to prevent similar issues in other dormitories.

sections.label: Westlite Jalan Tukang unrest and COVID-19
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Manpower about reasons for worker unhappiness and unrest, delays in COVID-19 isolation and treatment, and enforcement action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what were the main reasons for the unhappiness of foreign workers at the Westlite Jalan Tukang Dormitory leading to the unrest on 12 October 2021; (b) what measures have since been taken by the Ministry to ensure that conditions have improved and that the previous conditions will not recur; and (c) whether any action will be taken against the dormitory operators, employers of the workers or service suppliers for any neglect or omission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what are the reasons for the delays in isolation and treatment of COVID-19 infected workers, the extensive cross infection of workers, the serving of food unfit for consumption and the relatively low vaccination rate of workers at the Westlite Jalan Tukang dormitory; (b) what enforcement action will be taken against the operators, employers or food caterers; and (c) whether the Ministry has received and acted upon similar complaints from workers in other dormitories.

sections.label: DRF and CRF recovery beds
sections.summary: The 45 DRFs and three CRFs together have a total of 11,000 recovery beds.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The 45 DRFs and three CRFs together have a total of 11,000 recovery beds.

sections.label: Dormitory Recovery Programme workers
sections.summary: The dormitory operator checks on workers regularly, and over 17,000 workers have gone through the Dormitory Recovery Programme and safely recovered.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The dormitory operator also checks on them regularly.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: So far, over 17,000 workers have gone through the Dormitory Recovery Programme and have safely recovered.

sections.label: Hospital admission rate
sections.summary: Fewer than 0.2% needed to be admitted to the hospital.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In fact, fewer than 0.2% needed to be admitted to the hospital.

sections.label: Mass testing at Sembcorp Marine
sections.summary: After a sharp increase in COVID-19 cases on 10 October, Sembcorp Marine and ACE mass tested on 12 October, yielding 278 positive cases needing conveyance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: In response to the sharp increase in the number of COVID-19 cases on 10 October, Sembcorp Marine and ACE carried out a mass testing exercise on 12 October at the worksite and dormitory which yielded another 278 COVID-19-positive cases that needed to be conveyed from the dormitory to a CRF if they were vaccinated, or to another appropriate isolation facility if they were unvaccinated.

sections.label: Sembcorp Marine food hygiene concerns
sections.summary: Workers raised food quality and hygiene concerns at Sembcorp Marine; the Ministry asked the employer to address complaints and the Singapore Food Agency is investigating the caterer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Workers also raised concerns about the quality and hygiene standards of food provided by Sembcorp Marine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We take this very seriously and have asked the employer to address the complaints.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Ministry will not hesitate to take actions against any errant employer who fails to ensure workers' access to safe food.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The Singapore Food Agency is also investigating the food safety practices of this particular caterer.

sections.label: Dormitory Recovery Programme recoveries
sections.summary: More than 17,000 migrant workers have recovered under the Dormitory Recovery Programme with partners' support and hard work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: More than 17,000 migrant workers have recovered under the Dormitory Recovery Programme with the support and hard work of all these partners.

sections.label: Number of dormitories
sections.summary: There are 1,300 dormitories, big and small.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The reality is that we have 1,300 dormitories, big and small.

sections.label: Community visits and recreation centre access
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng visited a Hindu temple with migrant workers; community visits will increase to 3,000 workers a week and vaccinated dormitory workers can go to recreation centres more often.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Minister Tan See Leng himself visited one of the Hindu temples with many of our migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: And we are going to increase that number to 3,000 workers a week, especially with this festivity of Deepavali coming along, many of them will be looking forward to community visits as well.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Progressively, as we stabilise the dormitory recovery process, as the community also gets adjusted to Home Recovery Programme, as we move more and more into the endemic state, I believe that we can gradually reopen with a lot more numbers to allow our workers to access more community facilities.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We are also liberalising the number of times our vaccinated workers in the dormitories can go to the recreation centres as well.

sections.label: Vaccination requirement for incoming workers
sections.summary: A requirement exists to bring in only vaccinated workers, so the question asks why certain workers were not vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I know there is a requirement to bring in only vaccinated workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: So, in this instance, why were certain numbers of workers not vaccinated?

sections.label: Backlog cleared after 13 October
sections.summary: After 13 October, 70% had been conveyed by that night and the rest of the backlog was cleared by the next morning, 14 October, when other NGOs came in.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: When the situation had calmed down – after 13 October, by that night, as I said, 70% had been conveyed; and by the next morning, by 14 October, all the rest of the backlog had been cleared – this was when the rest of the NGOs came in.

sections.label: Vaccination rule for work pass holders
sections.summary: From 1 November, only fully vaccinated work pass holders are allowed to enter Singapore for work.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: Members would also have read from our previous announcement that from today, 1 November onwards, only work pass holders who are fully vaccinated will be allowed to enter Singapore for work.

sections.label: Migrant worker catered food guidelines
sections.summary: A 2015 survey found most workers felt food was unsatisfactory and unclean, raising whether SFA catered food guidelines apply to migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But in general, on food quality for migrant workers, there have been concerns about this going back for years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There was a survey, for example, in 2015, that talked about how the majority of workers felt the food was unsatisfactory, unclean and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, do those SFA guidelines for catered food supplied to Singaporeans also apply to catered food supplied to migrant workers?

sections.label: FWMOMCare app for foreign workers
sections.summary: The FWMOMCare app can be downloaded by all foreign workers onto their smart phones.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: First, we have now the FWMOMCare app, which is an app that all foreign workers can download onto their smart phones.

sections.label: Migrant Worker Ambassadors network
sections.summary: The Migrant Workers' Centre has established a network of Migrant Worker Ambassadors across the different dormitories.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: The third is that the Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC) has established a network of what we call Migrant Worker Ambassadors who are scattered throughout all the different dormitories.

sections.label: Employers' duty on worker food
sections.summary: Employers are told they must provide food of decent quality and hygiene standard for their workers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: This is where we need to communicate to them that there are avenues they can seek redress from.

sentences.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
sentences.text: We will also take this chance to impress on all employers that it is their responsibility and their obligation to make sure that they provide food of decent quality and hygiene standard that their workers can consume.
